quests.instruction: In a game of tag, Max runs after Ali to touch him. What is Max doing?
quests.hint: He moves quickly, and he follows someone who is also moving.
quests.explanation: Chase means to run after someone or something to catch it.
quests.funFact: Kittens and puppies practise chasing when they play.

quests.instruction: Noor crouches behind the sofa so nobody can see her. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: She wants to stay out of sight.
quests.explanation: Hide means to put yourself or something where it cannot be seen.
quests.funFact: An octopus can hide by changing its colour to match the rocks around it.

quests.instruction: In a game, Dev covers his eyes and counts, then goes around the house looking for his friends. What is he doing?
quests.hint: He is trying to find people who are out of sight.
quests.explanation: Seek means to look for someone or something. In the game of hide-and-seek, one child hides and the other seeks.
quests.funFact: Hide-and-seek is played by children in many parts of the world.

quests.instruction: Four children line up and try to be the first to reach the tree. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: Everyone is trying to get there first.
quests.explanation: Race means to try to be faster than other people over a distance.
quests.funFact: Some races, like relay races, are won by a whole team.

quests.instruction: Hana is the first to cross the finish line, so she will ___ the race.
quests.hint: She came first.
quests.explanation: Win means to be the best or first in a game or race.
quests.funFact: The ancient Olympic Games gave winners crowns made of olive leaves.

quests.instruction: Ravi's team scores two goals, but the other team scores five. Ravi's team will ___ the match.
quests.hint: The other team has more goals.
quests.explanation: Lose means to not win. It can also mean you cannot find something that you had.
quests.funFact: A good sport shakes hands with the other team whether they win or lose.

quests.instruction: Mia is far from the goal, so she sends the ball to a teammate who is closer. What does she do?
quests.hint: The ball goes to a friend.
quests.explanation: Pass means to send the ball to a teammate. Shoot means to try to score.
quests.funFact: Good passing is what makes a team strong, even more than one star player.

quests.instruction: Leo is right in front of the net and kicks the ball hard toward it. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: He wants the ball to go into the goal himself.
quests.explanation: Shoot means to kick or throw a ball toward the goal, to try to score.
quests.funFact: In basketball, you also shoot, but you throw the ball through a hoop.

quests.instruction: When the ball goes into the net, the team can ___.
quests.hint: A point is added to the board.
quests.explanation: Score means to get a point or a goal in a game.
quests.funFact: 'Score' can also mean twenty: people used to say 'four score' for eighty.

quests.instruction: Before gym class, Zoe reaches her arms high above her head to loosen her muscles. What does she do?
quests.hint: Her arms and body get longer.
quests.explanation: Stretch means to make your body or something else longer or wider by pulling.
quests.funFact: A rubber band can stretch a long way, but it will break if you pull too hard.

quests.instruction: Tom folds his body forward until his fingers touch his toes. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: His body makes an angle, but he does not get longer.
quests.explanation: Bend means to curve or fold your body or an object so that it is not straight.
quests.funFact: A bendy straw has a special part that lets it bend without breaking.

quests.instruction: Ella walks along a narrow beam and stops herself from falling. What is she doing?
quests.hint: She keeps steady on a thin path.
quests.explanation: Balance means to keep your body steady so that you do not fall.
quests.funFact: Tiny parts inside your ears help your body balance.

quests.instruction: When Sam is tired, his mouth opens wide without him wanting it to. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Tiredness is a clue.
quests.explanation: Yawn means to open your mouth wide and breathe in deeply, often when you are tired.
quests.funFact: Yawns can be catching: seeing someone yawn often makes you yawn too.

quests.instruction: The pepper tickles Nina's nose, and air suddenly bursts out. What does she do?
quests.hint: It starts in the nose.
quests.explanation: Sneeze means to push air out of your nose and mouth suddenly and loudly.
quests.funFact: Covering your nose with your elbow when you sneeze helps keep germs from spreading.

quests.instruction: A drink goes down the wrong way, and Kofi makes a loud noise from his throat. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: The noise comes from his throat, not his nose.
quests.explanation: Cough means to push air out of your throat with a sudden sound.
quests.funFact: Coughing helps your body clear dust and small bits from your throat.

quests.instruction: A bright light shines, and Anu closes and opens her eyes quickly. What does she do?
quests.hint: Both eyes move together.
quests.explanation: Blink means to close and open both eyes very quickly.
quests.funFact: People blink many times a minute without ever noticing.

quests.instruction: The teacher asks, 'Do you understand?' and Arjun moves his head up and down to say yes. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: He answers without speaking.
quests.explanation: Nod means to move your head up and down to say yes or to agree.
quests.funFact: In some countries, people use different head movements to mean yes or no.

quests.instruction: Ivy closes just one eye for a moment as a friendly secret signal. What does she do?
quests.hint: Only one eye closes.
quests.explanation: Wink means to close one eye quickly, often to share a joke or secret.
quests.funFact: Blink uses both eyes, but wink uses only one.

quests.instruction: Raj puts a tiny seed into the soil and covers it up. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: The seed goes into the ground to grow later.
quests.explanation: Plant means to put seeds or small plants into the ground so they can grow.
quests.funFact: Some bean seeds can show small green shoots in just a few days.

quests.instruction: The soil is dry, so Meena gives the little seedling a drink from a can. What does she do?
quests.hint: The word is also the name of the liquid she is using.
quests.explanation: Water can be a verb as well as a noun. To water a plant is to give it water.
quests.funFact: Plants take in water through their roots.

quests.instruction: With sunshine and water, a small seed will slowly ___ into a tall plant.
quests.hint: It becomes bigger over time.
quests.explanation: Grow means to get bigger or taller as time goes by.
quests.funFact: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants in the world.

quests.instruction: At the beach, Max makes a deep hole in the sand with his spade. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: The hole goes down into the ground.
quests.explanation: Dig means to make a hole by moving earth or sand away.
quests.funFact: A mole digs tunnels underground with its strong front paws.

quests.instruction: Priya lifts some sand with a small cup and puts it into her bucket. What does she do?
quests.hint: She picks up a little at a time with a cup or spoon.
quests.explanation: Scoop means to lift something up with a spoon, cup or your hand.
quests.funFact: An ice-cream scoop makes the ice cream round.

quests.instruction: In autumn, Dad pulls a tool with long teeth across the lawn to bring the leaves together. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: His tool has long teeth like a comb.
quests.explanation: Rake means to gather or smooth things with a rake.
quests.funFact: Leaves change colour in autumn because the green colour inside them fades.

quests.instruction: The dog sees a stranger at the gate and makes a loud 'woof!' What does it do?
quests.hint: Each animal has its own special word for its noise.
quests.explanation: Bark means to make the short, loud sound that dogs make.
quests.funFact: Dogs can bark to warn their family or to say hello.

quests.instruction: The farmer hears a duck on the pond making its noisy call. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Ducks have their own special word.
quests.explanation: Quack means to make the call of a duck.
quests.funFact: A mother duck's quacks help her ducklings follow her in a line.

quests.instruction: The lion opens its mouth wide and makes a deep, loud sound that can be heard far away. What does it do?
quests.hint: The sound is deep, powerful and loud.
quests.explanation: Roar means to make a deep, loud sound, like a lion does.
quests.funFact: A lion's roar can carry for several kilometres.

quests.instruction: Morning routine: wake up, ___ your face, eat breakfast. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: This step comes between waking up and eating.
quests.explanation: Wash is the action you do with water to be clean. A morning routine puts it before breakfast.
quests.funFact: A routine is a set of actions that you do in the same order each day.

quests.instruction: When Leo comes home from school, Mum says, '___ your shoes at the door.'
quests.hint: You go from wearing the shoes to not wearing them.
quests.explanation: Take off means to remove clothes or shoes. Put on is the opposite.
quests.funFact: In many countries, people take off their shoes before they go into a home.

quests.instruction: Before you go to sleep, put your book away and ___ off the lamp.
quests.hint: A light has an on and off button.
quests.explanation: Switch off means to stop something that uses power, such as a light or a TV.
quests.funFact: Turning off lights when you leave a room saves energy.
